A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WiserUI-Bench study. Their complete text, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison; relocated material was matched across versions.

before.justification: v4 reports original evaluations of nine MLLMs on UI/UX selection and interpretation, reasoning-strategy experiments, and qualitative analyses (Tables 2–4 and appendices).

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and adds evaluations of four models on both main tasks (Tables 2 and 4, Figure 5).

M1.justification: The benchmark design, selection and interpretation procedures, prompting strategies, and GPT-4o-based interpretation evaluator remain unchanged. Expanded curation explanations and additional evaluated models do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 300 UI pairs and 684 expert interpretations, spanning 11 page types, 13 industry domains, and two device types. The two tasks and represented evaluation scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 substantially expand the evaluated comparator set from nine to thirteen MLLMs, adding GPT-5.1, Claude 4.5 Sonnet, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, and Qwen3-VL-8B. Existing models and the reasoning-strategy comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce Qwen3-VL 30B-A3B/8B configurations, GPT-5.1 with reasoning effort set to none, and Claude 4.5 Sonnet with thinking disabled (Appendix B.1). Existing sample sizes, prompts, temperature, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The diagnostic analyses of difficulty across UI-element categories and cognitive UX dimensions extend to four additional models (Table 2 and Figure 5). Reasoning-strategy analyses and all main-text and appendix case studies retain their existing experimental evidence.

E5.justification: The three-run selection protocol, averaged reporting, and appendix standard-deviation table are unchanged. Evaluator validation remains 1,000 samples, 83.0% accuracy, and Cohen's kappa 0.66. No uncertainty rows are added for the new models.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 4 and Figure 5 substantially expand results across both tasks. GPT-5.1 reports 58.50% average selection accuracy, 33.33% consistent accuracy, and 68.71% interpretation recall. Claude 4.5 Sonnet becomes the instance-recall leader at 80.33%, versus the previous leader's 78.67%. Earlier models' table scores and appendix Tables 6–8 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The metric definitions and UX-law framework are unchanged. Neither version introduces new mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and central finding of limited behavior-aware UI/UX understanding. The additional models support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly interprets selection and explanation as related but dissociable capabilities and qualifies category-level generalizations. Appendix B.3.2 newly attributes low lexical scores mainly to verbosity and vocabulary differences, motivating semantic recall. The cultural, interactive-UI, and dataset-size limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 names OpenCV and Gemini-assisted cleanup, expanding the earlier automated/manual-refinement description without establishing changed benchmark images. Appendix B.1 adds model identifiers. Section 9 specifies source-URL, annotation, and processing-script distribution under a noncommercial license, but removes v4's explicit GitHub link.

R1.justification: v5 adds references for GPT-5.1, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Qwen3-VL, and OpenCV. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing UI evaluation and behavior-simulation research remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify annotation, interpretation metrics, results, and data-release practices. v5 also adds acknowledgments and an author affiliation note. The overall section order and narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 gain model rows, Figure 5 becomes a wider chart with revised colors and legend, and Figure 4 receives visual adjustments. Main-text displays reflow, while appendix Tables 5–8 and Figures 8–24 remain visually identical apart from page numbering.

improvement.justification: The additional models test whether benchmark difficulty persists in newer systems, while preprocessing and configuration disclosures improve transparency. These provide a limited quality gain without changing the benchmark or its validation. Removing the explicit repository link and leaving uncertainty tables unextended weaken reproducibility, but do not outweigh the broader empirical evidence and clearer documentation.
